_IPV4 = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?![\d.])")
# IPv6 in full (six groups or more, so a time like 21:05:03 is left alone)
# or shortened with "::" (fe80::1, ::1).
_IPV6 = re.compile(r"(?<![\w:])(?:(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}:){5,7}[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}"
                   r"|[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}::[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}[0-9A-Fa-f])(?![\w:])")
_MAC = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9A-Fa-f])(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}[:-]){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?![0-9A-Fa-f])")
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]{1,64}@[\w-]{1,63}(?:\.[\w-]{1,63})+")
# A supporter key pasted into a report would be the one thing that could tie it to a donation.
_SUPPORTER = re.compile(r"(?i)\bDS1-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}")
_KEYVAL = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(user(?:name)?|pass(?:word)?|pwd|token|key|api_key|apikey|secret|"
                     r"auth|sid|session|mac|play_token|login)(\s*[=:]\s*)([^\s&'\",;]+)")


def _not_an_address(text: str) -> bool:
    """Loopback - or the app's own test build's version, which has four
    numbers too ("1.6.0.123": the version and the build's run)."""
    from .. import __version__
    base = ".".join(__version__.split(".")[:3])
    return text.startswith("127.") or text.startswith(base + ".")


def scrub(text: str, personal: Iterable[str] = ()) -> str:
    """*text* without anything that identifies a stream or a person."""
    # Whole addresses first (a login or a name inside one goes with it),
    # then the person's own values, longest first (a name inside another).
    out = _URL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}://<address>", text or "")
    for value in sorted({v.strip() for v in personal if v and len(v.strip()) >= 3}, key=len, reverse=True):
        out = re.sub(re.escape(value), "<private>", out, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
    out = _SUPPORTER.sub("<supporter key>", out)
    out = _EMAIL.sub("<email>", out)
    out = _MAC.sub("<mac>", out)
    out = _IPV6.sub("<ip>", out)
    out = _IPV4.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if _not_an_address(m.group(0)) else "<ip>", out)
    out = _KEYVAL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}<hidden>", out)
    home = os.path.expanduser("~")
    if len(home) > 1:
        out = out.replace(home, "~")
    try:
        user = getpass.getuser()
    except Exception:
        user = ""
    if user and len(user) >= 3:
        out = re.sub(rf"(?<![\w]){re.escape(user)}(?![\w])", "<user>", out)
    return out


def personal_values(playlists: Iterable[dict], channels: Iterable[str] = (),
                    titles: Iterable[str] = ()) -> list[str]:
    """What the app knows to be someone's: sources' names, servers, logins
    and boxes; channel names; titles watched."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for p in playlists or []:
        for key in ("name", "server", "username", "password", "mac", "epg_url"):
            v = str(p.get(key) or "")
            if v:
                out.append(v)
                if key == "server":
                    host = re.sub(r"^[a-z]+://", "", v).split("/")[0].split("@")[-1].split(":")[0]
                    out.append(host)
    out += [str(c) for c in channels if c]
    out += [str(t) for t in titles if t]
    return out

#: An address inside free text - the pattern the error report takes whole
#: addresses out by (core/report.py uses this one).
URL_IN_TEXT = re.compile(r"\b([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]{1,15})://[^\s'\"<>()\[\]]+")

def _post(url: str, body: bytes, timeout: float) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
    """POST JSON with requests, whose certificates (certifi) travel with the
    app: urllib asks the system's OpenSSL for them, and a bundled Python on
    macOS has none, so every report failed there."""
    from .. import __version__
    from ._lazy_requests import requests
    r = requests.post(url, data=body, timeout=timeout, headers={
        "Content-Type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
        "User-Agent": f"dopeIPTV/{__version__}", "X-Dopeiptv-Report": "1",
        **build_check.headers()})
    return r.status_code, r.content

def send_status(kind: str, text: str, timeout: float = 15.0, endpoint: str | None = None,
                extra: dict | None = None) -> int:
    """send(), with the site's answer: its HTTP status - 409 for a reply to
    an answer whose thread is closed - or 0 when nothing reached it (never
    from a modified build)."""
    from .. import __version__
    if not build_check.allowed():
        log.info("report: not sent - not an official build")
        return 0
    extra = extra or {}
    fields = {"kind": kind if kind in ("error", "crash", "feedback") else "feedback",
              "version": __version__, "os": platform.system(),
              "text": (text or "")[:MAX_TEXT]}
    # What feedback is about (a topic, an area, how often) and "supporter":
    # "yes" from a supporter (read first): single words from a short list.
    fields.update({k: v for k, v in extra.items()
                   if k in ("topic", "area", "often", "supporter")
                   and isinstance(v, str) and v.isalpha() and len(v) <= 12})
    # The hash of the code this computer keeps to be told the answers - and
    # for a reply to an answer, the same hash as the thread it belongs to.
    for key in ("reply", "thread"):
        if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(extra.get(key) or "")):
            fields[key] = str(extra[key])
    # UTF-8 as it is (an escaped "å" is six bytes), and cut to what the site
    # takes - a long log once made the whole report too big to be kept.
    body = json.dumps(fields, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
    if len(body) > MAX_BODY:
        fields["text"] = _fit(fields["text"], len(fields["text"].encode("utf-8")) - (len(body) - MAX_BODY) - 64)
        body = json.dumps(fields, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
    try:
        status, _data = _post(endpoint or ENDPOINT, body, timeout)
    except Exception as e:
        log.info("report: not sent (%s)", type(e).__name__)
        return 0
    if not 200 <= status < 300:
        log.info("report: not sent (HTTP %s)", status)
        return status
    log.info("report: sent (%s%s)", kind, ", a reply" if "thread" in fields else "")
    return status

_URL = re.compile(r"\b([a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9+.-]{1,15})://[^\s'\"<>()\[\]]+")
_IPV4 = re.compile(r"(?<![\d.])(?:\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}(?![\d.])")
# IPv6 as the app's core/report.py finds it: in full (six groups or more, so
# a time like 21:05:03 is left alone) or shortened with "::" (fe80::1, ::1).
_IPV6 = re.compile(r"(?<![\w:])(?:(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}:){5,7}[0-9A-Fa-f]{1,4}"
                   r"|[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}::[0-9A-Fa-f:]{0,30}[0-9A-Fa-f])(?![\w:])")
_EMAIL = re.compile(r"[\w.+-]{1,64}@[\w-]{1,63}(?:\.[\w-]{1,63})+")
_MAC = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9A-Fa-f])(?:[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}[:-]){5}[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}(?![0-9A-Fa-f])")
_KEYVAL = re.compile(r"(?i)\b(user(?:name)?|pass(?:word)?|pwd|token|key|secret|auth|mac)(\s*[=:]\s*)([^\s&'\",;]+)")

_SUPPORTER = re.compile(r"(?i)\bDS1-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}")


def scrub(text: str) -> str:
    out = _URL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}://<address>", text or "")
    out = _SUPPORTER.sub("<supporter key>", out)
    out = _EMAIL.sub("<email>", out)
    out = _MAC.sub("<mac>", out)
    out = _IPV6.sub("<ip>", out)
    out = _IPV4.sub(lambda m: m.group(0) if m.group(0).startswith("127.") else "<ip>", out)
    return _KEYVAL.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1)}{m.group(2)}<hidden>", out)

def hkdf(ikm: bytes, salt: bytes, info: bytes, length: int) -> bytes:
    """HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869)."""
    prk = hmac.new(salt or b"\0" * 32, ikm, hashlib.sha256).digest()
    out, block = b"", b""
    counter = 1
    while len(out) < length:
        block = hmac.new(prk, block + info + bytes([counter]), hashlib.sha256).digest()
        out += block
        counter += 1
    return out[:length]


def derive(raw: bytes) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    """(slot, key) for a code: the slot the site keeps it under (64 hex)
    and the encryption key, each from its own HKDF label - knowing one says
    nothing about the other."""
    slot = hkdf(raw, _SALT, b"slot", 32).hex()
    return slot, hkdf(raw, _SALT, b"key", 32)

def seal(key: bytes, doc: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    """The snapshot as the site keeps it: a format byte, a random nonce and
    the compressed JSON, encrypted and authenticated."""
    plain = zlib.compress(_canon(doc).encode("utf-8"), 6)
    nonce = secrets.token_bytes(12)
    head = bytes([FORMAT])
    return head + nonce + aead.encrypt(key, nonce, plain, _AAD + head)

#: A message's plain text is padded up to one of these, so the sizes the
#: relay sees say little about what was sent.
_PAD = (192, 384, 768, 1536)

def seal(key: bytes, room: str, msg: dict[str, Any]) -> bytes:
    """*msg* as the relay passes it: a format byte, a random nonce, and the
    padded JSON, encrypted and tied to the room."""
    text = json.dumps(msg, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
    size = next((p for p in _PAD if p >= len(text) + 2), 0)
    if not size:
        raise ValueError("message too long")
    plain = struct.pack(">H", len(text)) + text + b"\0" * (size - 2 - len(text))
    nonce = secrets.token_bytes(12)
    head = bytes([FORMAT])
    return head + nonce + aead.encrypt(key, nonce, plain, _AAD + head + bytes.fromhex(room))

def add(self, url: str, title: str, icon_url: str | None,
            key: str, kind: str, extra: dict | None = None) -> None:
        # Private viewing: nothing played is kept - nor the private playback
        # going on after it ends (a live channel's reconnect starts it again).
        if not url or privacy.playback_private(kind, key):
            return
        # str() both sides: providers mix int and str ids, and a key that
        # round-tripped through JSON elsewhere may come back the other type -
        # a raw == then missed and the same title stacked up as duplicates.
        self.entries = [e for e in self.entries
                        if not (str(e.get("_key")) == str(key)
                                and e.get("_kind") == kind)]
        entry = {
            "name": title, "stream_icon": icon_url,
            "_url": url, "_key": key, "_kind": kind,
            "_watched_at": datetime.now().isoformat(),
        }
        # Carry through extra channel fields (e.g. stream_id, tv_archive) so a
        # live channel replayed from History keeps its catch-up/timeshift.
        if extra:
            entry.update({k: v for k, v in extra.items() if v is not None})
        self.entries.insert(0, entry)
        self.entries = self.entries[:self.MAX_ENTRIES]
        self._save()

def user_agent() -> str:
    """``dopeIPTV/1.4.4 (Windows; AMD64)``: what the app is, which version
    it runs and on what - all the site learns of an update check or an
    update, and how it tells them from a browser."""
    return f"dopeIPTV/{VERSION} ({platform.system() or sys.platform}; {platform.machine() or '?'})"

#: Sent with every request to dopeiptv.org: official, modified or source.
HEADER = "X-dopeIPTV-Build"
OFFICIAL, MODIFIED, SOURCE = "official", "modified", "source"

def lan_address() -> str:
    """This machine's address on the LAN, as the Chromecast will see it.

    A UDP socket is 'connected' to an outside address to find out which
    interface the kernel would route through - nothing is sent, and it is the
    only way that survives a machine with several interfaces (Wi-Fi, Ethernet,
    a VPN, Docker) where the hostname resolves to the wrong one.
    """
    s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    try:
        s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80))
        return s.getsockname()[0]
    except Exception:
        return "127.0.0.1"
    finally:
        s.close()

# -- statistics -----------------------------------------------------------------
# One line per page view (only / and /help/ are logged here), read every
# quarter hour by donate/stats_collect.py, which keeps nothing but counts per
# day for the admin page. The address is in the log, as in any access log;
# newsyslog (DEPLOY.md "Statistics") keeps a week of it.
log_format iptv_stats escape=json
    '{"ip":"$http_x_real_ip","t":"$time_iso8601","m":"$request_method",'
    '"u":"$request_uri","s":$status,"r":"$http_referer","a":"$http_user_agent",'
    '"l":"$iptv_lang"}';

def _new_visit(visits: Visits, day: str, vid: str, t: int, ip: str, ua: str, db) -> dict:
    name, version = browser_of(ua)
    v = {"id": vid, "start": t, "end": t, "browser": name, "bv": version,
         "os": os_version_of(ua), "device": device_of(ua),
         "country": (db.country(ip) if db is not None else "") or "",
         "returning": visits.before(day, vid), "pages": [], "time": 0,
         "downloads": [], "events": []}
    visits.day(day).append(v)
    return v
